title: Price-Per-Use of Big Purchases
dataSources: Micro-spend transactions (`microspend:txn`), no-spend days (`nospend:day`), price-per-use items (`priceperuse:item`), cash-back rewards (`cashback:reward`).
app: Bank-transaction exports categorised for micro-spending, no-spend-day trackers, price-per-use logs, and cash-back / rewards feeds — sent to Splunk HEC via scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=priceperuse:item
| stats latest(price) as price, sum(uses) as uses by item
| eval cost_per_use=round(price/uses,2)
| sort - cost_per_use
description: Divides the cost of your bigger purchases by how many times you have used them, exposing the real value of each.
value: Cost-per-use vindicates a well-used splurge and shames the gadget in the cupboard, guiding smarter future buys.
implementation: Log uses of tracked items into `index=personal`; compute cost-per-use per item.
visualization: Bar chart of cost-per-use by purchase.
grandmaExplanation: It works out how much each big purchase costs per time you use it, showing which were worth the money.
